Rayagada (Odisha) [India], November 17 (ANI): The Rayagada district administration in Odisha has identified around 55 landslide-prone villages for pre-emptive evacuation and stepped up preparedness ahead of Cyclone Akvan, which is likely to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 19 or 20, District Magistrate Ashutosh Kulkarni said on Tuesday.
Kulkarni told reporters that Rayagada, located in southern Odisha along the Andhra Pradesh border, has been issued yellow and orange warnings for November 18, 19 and 20, with heavy rainfall forecast in the region.
'Since we have an upcoming Cyclone Akvan, which is going to make landfall either on November 19 or 20, with the point of landfall somewhere in Andhra Pradesh, as predicted by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), and given that we are in the southern part of Odisha bordering Andhra Pradesh, heavy rainfall has been forecast. Accordingly, we have yellow and orange warnings for three days, November 18, 19, and 20, and we have made our preparations accordingly,' he stated.
Speaking on the preparedness of the cyclone, he informed that a district-level meeting was conducted and departments have been instructed to carry out the tasks assigned to them. He also noted that atleast 55 villages were identified as landslide-prone and pre-emptive evacuation will be conducted as a preventive measure.
'Today, we also conducted a district-level preparatory meeting, and all line departments have been instructed to carry out their assigned tasks. There are about 55 villages that we have identified as landslide-prone, and we will conduct a pre-emptive evacuation of those areas as a preventive measure. We also have several other habitations along a river that may face flooding in the event of excessive rainfall,' he said.
The District Magistrate further said that the Harabhangi and Badanalla dam projects had started releasing water to lower their reservoir levels and create capacity to manage excess rainfall.
'The two dam projects, Harabhangi and Badanalla, have started releasing water to ensure that their reservoirs are emptied to a certain extent. Therefore, we do not expect immediate flooding, and in case there is excessive rainfall, the dams will be able to hold back water for a few hours so that we can carry out evacuations in the lower reaches of the river as well...' he added.
Meanwhile, IMD Hyderabad Meteorologist GNRS Srinivas said Cyclone Akvan is likely to affect Telangana after crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast, with four eastern districts placed under an orange alert for November 20.
Speaking in Hyderabad, Srinivas said the cyclone, which formed over the southeast Bay of Bengal three days ago, had intensified into a cyclone by the previous evening and was likely to strengthen further into a severe cyclone over the West Central Bay of Bengal by Tuesday evening or night.
He said the system was likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Thune on the morning or afternoon of November 20, and its effects could also be felt in Telangana.
'Some of the eastern districts in Telangana are put under orange alert on the 20th. These districts are Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad, and Suryapet... By tomorrow evening, the picture will be clearer. And accordingly, the forecast for Telangana can be modified...' he said.
Srinivas said the weather forecast for Telangana could be revised as the cyclone's movement and intensity become clearer. (ANI)

articles.full_text:
Bhubaneswar: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Tuesday issued a Cyclone Alert (Orange Message) for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts as Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’, centred about 770 km south of Gopalpur, is likely to intensify into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by November 19.
The cyclonic storm, over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, moved north-northwards at a speed of 3 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred near latitude 12.4°N and longitude 85.6°E at 8.30 pm on Tuesday, according to the IMD’s latest bulletin issued at 10.30 pm.
The system is very likely to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm by Wednesday morning (November 18). It is likely to strengthen further into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by the evening of November 19 while moving northwestwards.
Continuing its northwestward movement, the system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon on November 20 as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 120-130 kmph and gusts reaching 145 kmph.

articles.full_text:
Cyclone Akvan, churning over the central and west-central Bay of Bengal, has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and slightly altered its trajectory due to atmospheric pressure changes, putting both Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha on high alert.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the storm remained virtually stationary for several hours on Monday before beginning a slow northwestward movement. As of the latest tracking, Akvan is positioned roughly 590 km east of Chennai, 650 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 650 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, and about 780 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha.
Intensification and Landfall Forecast
Meteorologists warn that while the system has shifted its track slightly, its destructive potential remains unchanged. Gathering strength over warm ocean waters, Akvan is projected to escalate into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by the evening of November 19. Continuing northwest, it is expected to make landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam along the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts around noon on November 20. At landfall, sustained wind speeds are forecast to reach 120–130 km/h, with violent gusts peaking at 145 km/h.
Marking the third cyclonic system to form in the Bay of Bengal in just three weeks, Akvan follows a string of recent storms that battered the Andhra coastline. An Orange Warning has been issued for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts, and fishermen have been strictly advised not to venture into the sea until November 21.
Odisha Braces for Outer-Band Fury
Although Cyclone Akvan will bypass a direct landfall in Odisha, its expansive outer cloud bands will trigger widespread adverse weather across the state before the system weakens into a depression by the night of November 21. Southern districts—including Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, and Nabarangpur—will bear the brunt of the storm’s peripheral impact.
The Regional Meteorological Centre has issued a phased warning schedule for Odisha:
November 17–18: Light to moderate rain and thundershowers are likely in Balasore, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Cuttack, Mayurbhanj, Gajapati, Ganjam, Puri, Khordha, and Nayagarh.
November 18–19 (Yellow Warning): Heavy rainfall is expected at isolated places in Gajapati, Ganjam, and Puri. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds reaching 40–50 km/h are forecast across 15 coastal, northern, and southern districts.
November 19–20 (Orange Warning): Weather conditions will deteriorate sharply across the state. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is likely in Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Gajapati, Ganjam, and Puri. Heavy rain will also lash interior and northern pockets including Angul, Dhenkanal, Keonjhar, and Mayurbhanj, accompanied by squally winds of 50–60 km/h.
November 20–21 (Orange Warning): Intense downpours will shift toward southern and western Odisha, with extremely heavy rainfall warnings in place for Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati, and Ganjam. Heavy rain is also predicted for Sambalpur, Subarnapur, Balangir, and Kalahandi.
Post-Landfall Outlook & Advisory
Widespread rain will persist through November 22 before tapering off to isolated light-to-moderate showers on November 23 and 24, with no weather warnings issued for those days.
In light of the approaching squalls and heavy downpours, authorities have cautioned that standing crops, horticultural plantations, and trees face a high risk of damage, alongside potential disruptions to power lines and communication networks caused by falling branches.
